# Auto-generated `update_json`/`render_json` island bridges are 100% non-functional

Found 2026-08-12 while auditing `test/stdlib/test_island_bridges.march` as part of
wiring the 37 unwired `test/stdlib/*.march` files into CI
(see `specs/progress/2026-08-11-test-stdlib-march-files-not-in-ci.md`, the completed
version of the todo that started this work).

## The bug

`lib/desugar/desugar.ml:2601` (`gen_island_bridges`) auto-generates `update_json`
and `render_json` for any module shaped like `type State = {...}` + `type Msg = ...`
+ `derive Json for State` + `derive Json for Msg` + `update`/`render` functions —
exactly the shape the feature's own doc comment describes as its trigger condition.
The generated bodies decode both JSON strings through a single bare call,
`from_json(sjv)` / `from_json(mjv)`, relying on the typechecker inferring the right
concrete type per call site (comment at `lib/desugar/desugar.ml:2605-2608`).

That reasoning is correct at typecheck time but wrong at both runtime paths that
actually execute the call:

- **Interpreted** (`march test`, `dune exec march --`): `derive Json`'s `from_json`
  is a bare name rebound in the environment by each `derive Json` declaration
  (last one wins — this is the already-tracked bug in
  `specs/2026-07-31-json-from-json-dispatch-design.md`). Since `Msg`'s derive comes
  after `State`'s, **both** `from_json(sjv)` and `from_json(mjv)` call `Msg`'s
  decoder. Decoding `sjv` (a `State`-shaped JSON object, no `"tag"` field) with
  `Msg`'s variant decoder always fails, so `update_json` silently falls through to
  its `_ -> state_json` branch and returns the **input unchanged** — every call
  looks like a no-op. Confirmed with a minimal repro (module with just
  `State`/`Msg`/`update`/`render`): `update_json("{\"count\":5}",
  "{\"tag\":\"Increment\"}")` returns `"{\"count\":5}"` instead of incrementing.

- **Compiled** (`march --compile`, `forge build`): `lib/tir/mono.ml`'s
  `return_position_single_impl` fallback (comment at `lib/tir/mono.ml:616-628`)
  only resolves a `from_json` call when exactly one impl is registered
  module-wide. With both `State` and `Msg` deriving Json, compiling the same
  minimal repro **fails to compile**: `error: ambiguous interface-method call to
  ` from_json`: 2 implementations are in scope (JsonFrom$Msg.from_json,
  JsonFrom$State.from_json)`.

So the island-bridge feature cannot work for its own advertised use case in
either execution path — not "sometimes wrong," but unconditionally broken any
time a module has both a `State` and a `Msg` type deriving Json, which is
required for the bridges to be generated at all.

## Why this wasn't caught

`test/stdlib/test_island_bridges.march` (161 tests, 7 covering this exact
behavior) is one of the 37 stdlib test files that ran under no CI runner. Its
`describe "auto-generated update_json"` / `"render_json"` / `"round-trip"` blocks
would have failed the moment they were wired in.

## Why this isn't a test-file fix

Unlike the plain `from_json` dispatch bug (worked around in
`test/stdlib/test_derive_json.march` by capturing each type's decode result in a
top-level `let` right after that type's own `derive Json`, per the interim
guidance in the design doc), there is no equivalent workaround available from
*test* code here: `update_json`/`render_json` are generated by the compiler
itself, inside the module under test — a test file has no way to intercept or
rewrite their bodies.

A real fix belongs in `gen_island_bridges` (or the shared `from_json` dispatch
mechanism it depends on). One direction worth scoping: since `gen_island_bridges`
knows statically that the first call site must decode to `State` and the second
to `Msg`, it could generate small per-type helper closures positioned immediately
after each type's own `derive Json` (mirroring the interim-guidance workaround),
so each closure captures the correct environment-bound `from_json` at creation
time — but this would only fix the **interpreted** path; the **compiled** path's
ambiguity error is a separate, TIR-level check (`lib/tir/mono.ml`) that would
need its own fix (e.g. having `gen_island_bridges` emit calls that are
unambiguous by construction, rather than relying on `return_position_single_impl`
to disambiguate after the fact). A full fix likely wants the same design pass
scoped in `specs/2026-07-31-json-from-json-dispatch-design.md`, extended to cover
this call site.

## Current status

`test/stdlib/test_island_bridges.march` is left **unwired** (manual-only, `march
test test/stdlib/test_island_bridges.march`) pending this fix — it is the one
file of the original 37 not included in the new `test/dune` runtest rule, to
avoid landing a red (or falsely-green) CI check for a feature that does not
work. Its other 154 tests (everything except the 7 `update_json`/`render_json`
behavior tests) pass and were left as-is.
